name: g1-networked-destruction
description: CPU-side G1 gate fixture on the cross-brick bridge scene: a single column straddling the x = 32 brick boundary holds a beam that also spans both bricks. Client 0 cuts the seam column to detach the beam while both clients excavate opposite ends of the floor concurrently; client 0 also carves the falling beam again with a body-targeted cut while it is still moving. Passes only if every scripted cut commits (an early quiescence fails), the server and both clients agree on one canonical hash, the detached body's cells were owned across a brick boundary (span >= 2 bricks), each live client observes real beam displacement, the body-targeted cut lands, and the committed topology-event stream replayed from the tick-0 baseline reproduces the same hash. Run with --loss-percent 2 for the impaired-transport variant, which additionally requires the live clients to have observed motion datagrams delivered out of order.
